fact_text: Producing one ton of urea in Pakistan consumes roughly 27-28 units (MMBTU) of natural gas in total, making gas the dominant physical input.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Understanding Fatima Fertilizer: Business, Costs & 2026 Outlook' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Natural gas accounts for roughly 60-70% of the cost of producing urea, so gas pricing decisions flow almost directly into fertilizer company profits.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Understanding Fatima Fertilizer: Business, Costs & 2026 Outlook' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Fertilizer demand in Pakistan tracks population and cropped area rather than GDP, which is why the analyst treats it as a defensive, structurally non-declining demand base.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Understanding Fatima Fertilizer: Business, Costs & 2026 Outlook' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Pakistan's annual urea demand of about 6.0-6.7 million tons is closely matched by domestic capacity of roughly 6.5-7.0 million tons, so utilisation stays high and imports are only occasional.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Understanding Fatima Fertilizer: Business, Costs & 2026 Outlook' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Because local gas is priced on a largely fixed domestic formula, Pakistani urea sells far below imported urea, giving local producers room to pass gas-cost increases into bag prices instead of absorbing them.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Understanding Fatima Fertilizer: Business, Costs & 2026 Outlook' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst argues fertilizer profits and dividends hold up through currency devaluation episodes because both the main input (local gas) and the output price are set domestically.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Understanding Fatima Fertilizer: Business, Costs & 2026 Outlook' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Fatima Fertilizer is a joint venture of the Fatima Group and Arif Habib Group that produces urea, CAN and NP, and is the market leader in CAN and NP rather than being urea-only.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Understanding Fatima Fertilizer: Business, Costs & 2026 Outlook' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Pakistan's Fertilizer Policy 2001 attracted new plant investment by granting new entrants concessionary gas for ten years, which is how Fatima Fertilizer's full-spectrum plant came about.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Understanding Fatima Fertilizer: Business, Costs & 2026 Outlook' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Industry estimates put Fatima Fertilizer's share of Pakistan's urea market at roughly 14-18%.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Understanding Fatima Fertilizer: Business, Costs & 2026 Outlook' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Calcium ammonium nitrate (CAN) takes roughly 15 units of gas plus calcium per ton, and because it carries less nitrogen than urea farmers buy it at a discount to urea.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Understanding Fatima Fertilizer: Business, Costs & 2026 Outlook' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Fatima Fertilizer is the only producer of CAN in Pakistan, so this product line faces no direct domestic competitor.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Understanding Fatima Fertilizer: Business, Costs & 2026 Outlook' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: One ton of NP fertilizer takes about 12 units of gas plus 0.7 tons of imported phosphate rock, so NP costs rise with global phosphate prices.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Understanding Fatima Fertilizer: Business, Costs & 2026 Outlook' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: NP is priced at a discount to DAP in Pakistan and DAP itself is set by international prices because it is imported, so a global phosphate up-cycle lifts NP prices alongside NP costs.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Understanding Fatima Fertilizer: Business, Costs & 2026 Outlook' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst noted the 2021-2022 commodity super-cycle as an episode when globally dearer phosphate fertilizer lifted Fatima's NP margins rather than hurting them.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Understanding Fatima Fertilizer: Business, Costs & 2026 Outlook' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Fatima's main Sadiqabad plant in Rahim Yar Khan makes all three products, with capacity near 500,000 tons urea and 470,000 tons CAN a year, fed by 110 MMCFD of dedicated Mari gas.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Understanding Fatima Fertilizer: Business, Costs & 2026 Outlook' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: After the policy revision reported in February 2024 many fertilizer plants saw gas move from about PKR 580 to roughly PKR 1,600 per MMBTU, but plants contracted directly with Mari Energy stayed at PKR 580.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Understanding Fatima Fertilizer: Business, Costs & 2026 Outlook' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Fatima's Multan plant is supplied through the SNGPL pipeline under the Petroleum Policy PP-2012 regime at around USD 5.6 per MMBTU, roughly equivalent to the higher PKR 1,600 rate.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Understanding Fatima Fertilizer: Business, Costs & 2026 Outlook' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Fatima's Sheikhupura plant, with about 450,000 tons of urea capacity, sat on the SNGPL network running on imported RLNG, so gas price and supply problems repeatedly forced it to shut down.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Understanding Fatima Fertilizer: Business, Costs & 2026 Outlook' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The government allocated 52 MMSCFD of dedicated process gas from Mari's Ghazij and Shawal discoveries to Fatima's Sheikhupura plant at OGRA-regulated rates, which the analyst sees as a structural fix to that plant's viability.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Understanding Fatima Fertilizer: Business, Costs & 2026 Outlook' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Building the pipeline infrastructure for the new Sheikhupura gas allocation is expected to take about one and a half to two years before the plant can rely on it.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Understanding Fatima Fertilizer: Business, Costs & 2026 Outlook' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Fatima separated the Sheikhupura plant into wholly owned Fatima Fert Limited in July 2024, and a Multan plant demerger begun in January 2025 was approved by the Lahore High Court in November 2025 for transfer to Pak Arab Fertilizers.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Understanding Fatima Fertilizer: Business, Costs & 2026 Outlook' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst reads the corporate restructuring as improving transparency by letting each subsidiary be evaluated independently and opening the door to future options such as separate IPOs.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Understanding Fatima Fertilizer: Business, Costs & 2026 Outlook' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: On an illustrative 2026 scenario of about 1.0-1.1m tons urea, 0.8-0.9m tons CAN and 0.9m tons NP, the analyst modelled revenue near PKR 300bn with gross margins of 34-38%.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Understanding Fatima Fertilizer: Business, Costs & 2026 Outlook' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's 2026 scenario for Fatima Fertilizer put operating profit at roughly PKR 67-70bn and net profit at PKR 46-50bn, about PKR 20-23 per share.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Understanding Fatima Fertilizer: Business, Costs & 2026 Outlook' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Fatima Fertilizer receives roughly PKR 15-16bn of other income a year, generated by long-term investments such as mutual funds and sukuk.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Understanding Fatima Fertilizer: Business, Costs & 2026 Outlook' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: In Pakistan's largest privatisation in about two decades, concluded on 23 December 2025, an Arif Habib Corporation-led consortium acquired 51% of PIA for roughly PKR 135bn, with Fatima Fertilizer holding 34.1% of the consortium.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Understanding Fatima Fertilizer: Business, Costs & 2026 Outlook' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Fatima Fertilizer holds a 33.3% stake in National Resources Limited, a mineral explorer that has identified 16 mineral-rich locations across about 500 square kilometres, with drilling near Chagai indicating significant deposit potential.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Understanding Fatima Fertilizer: Business, Costs & 2026 Outlook' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Fatima Fertilizer shareholders approved PKR 7.66bn of REIT investments at the AGM of 22 September 2023, managed by Arif Habib Dolmen REIT Management, including PKR 4.1bn of new money into the Sapphire Bay Islamic REIT.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Understanding Fatima Fertilizer: Business, Costs & 2026 Outlook' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst reads Fatima's aviation, mining and real-estate stakes as a gradual move from pure fertilizer producer towards a broader conglomerate, supporting other income but adding non-core exposure.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Understanding Fatima Fertilizer: Business, Costs & 2026 Outlook' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Lotte Chemical Pakistan is the country's only large-scale producer of PTA, the chemical that the textile export industry and PET bottle and FMCG packaging makers depend on.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Lotte Chemicals Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Pakistan's PTA demand of roughly 700,000-800,000 tons a year exceeds Lotte's roughly 500,000 ton capacity, so its Port Qasim plant runs near full utilisation and the balance is imported.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Lotte Chemicals Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: PTA is made by processing paraxylene, which Lotte imports mostly from the Middle East and Asia at roughly 0.67 tons per ton of PTA, making it the dominant raw material.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Lotte Chemicals - Everything You Need to Know about Lotte Chemicals' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Making PTA is electricity-intensive at roughly 450-500 units per ton, so the power tariff is one of the most important variables in Lotte's cost structure.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Lotte Chemicals Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Lotte moved almost entirely from its captive gas power plant to the national grid after gas prices and captive power levies pushed its gas cost above PKR 4,000 per MMBTU from around PKR 1,200, making captive generation uneconomic.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Lotte Chemicals Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: At an assumed grid rate near 11 US cents a unit, electricity works out to roughly USD 50 per ton of PTA, with fixed costs such as salaries, maintenance and depreciation adding about USD 20-25 per ton.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Lotte Chemicals Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The PTA-paraxylene margin is only the price spread between product and feedstock, not profit per ton: electricity and fixed costs must still be deducted, so investors who read the spread as profit misjudge the business.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Lotte Chemicals Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Because electricity and fixed costs per ton barely move, a 50% rise in the PTA-paraxylene spread can roughly triple profit per ton, and a spread near zero pushes the company to break-even or losses.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Lotte Chemicals Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Lotte imports paraxylene at zero duty while finished PTA imports carry customs duty, additional customs duty and freight, so Lotte can price at import parity and capture that protection as margin.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Lotte Chemicals Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Because import duty protection is a percentage of price, the same 10% duty is worth about USD 70 per ton when the global product price is USD 700 but far more at USD 1,000, so the global price matters as much as the duty rate.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Lotte Chemicals Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: In Budget 2025 the government cut PTA customs duty from roughly 16% to 5% and took the additional customs duty from about 4% to zero under its IMF trade-liberalisation framework, weakening Lotte's historic duty protection.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Lotte Chemicals Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: With duties cut, imported PTA (especially Chinese material) lands in Pakistan at a lower cost, so the analyst treats further tariff rationalisation in coming budgets as a key structural risk to Lotte's margins.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Lotte Chemicals Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Lotte's new owners have shown interest in acquiring EPCL, effectively Pakistan's only large-scale PVC producer, with due diligence at an advanced stage and a share purchase agreement process initiated.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Lotte Chemicals Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: EPCL self-generates most of its roughly 54 MW electricity requirement from gas at about PKR 50 per unit, taking its annual power bill to around PKR 22bn, because it has no direct grid connection.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Lotte Chemicals Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Lotte's management estimates that connecting EPCL to optimised grid infrastructure after an acquisition could save about PKR 10bn a year, roughly PKR 7bn from the grid connection and PKR 3bn from renewables.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Lotte Chemicals Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Historical correlation between PTA and PVC margins is only about 0.3, so the analyst sees a PVC acquisition as a natural hedge that reduces Lotte's single-product dependency.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Lotte Chemicals Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Lotte has completed a 6.5 MW solar phase one, expects an 8-9 MW solar phase two by October 2026 and plans an 8 MW wind project on a 2028 timeline, alongside contract renegotiations targeting 15-30% savings.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Lotte Chemicals Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst works with a payback period of roughly two to three years for industrial solar and renewable energy investments.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Lotte Chemicals Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst argues cost optimisation is the most reliable lever for a company like Lotte whose margins swing with a global commodity spread it cannot control.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Lotte Chemicals Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: On analytical assumptions of about 400,000 tons of sales, the analyst modelled 2026 revenue of roughly PKR 83-85bn, gross margins of 9-11%, operating profit of PKR 6-7bn and net profit of PKR 3-4bn.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Lotte Chemicals Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: To forecast Lotte's margins the analyst tracks global PTA capacity additions, existing plant utilisation and China's production behaviour, since China dominates the global PTA market.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Lotte Chemicals Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: For 2026 the analyst saw a relatively positive signal in few major global PTA capacity additions plus China retiring some plants and lowering utilisation at others, which could support PTA-paraxylene spreads.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Lotte Chemicals Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst listed three developments that together hurt Lotte's profitability: a weaker PTA spread, far costlier captive gas after the levy, and the Budget 2025 duty reduction.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Lotte Chemicals - Everything You Need to Know about Lotte Chemicals' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: For FY26 the analyst modelled Lotte revenue of about PKR 85bn, operating profit of PKR 4-5bn and after-tax EPS in the PKR 1.5-2.5 range.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Lotte Chemicals - Everything You Need to Know about Lotte Chemicals' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: An earlier share purchase agreement to sell Lotte's stake to Lucky Core Industries at roughly PKR 30-35 per share lapsed, partly because the roughly USD 150m transaction ran into State Bank restrictions on outflows amid low reserves.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Lotte Chemicals - Everything You Need to Know about Lotte Chemicals' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Lotte's exit from Pakistan was completed in 2025 to a buyer group including Liberty Group, valuing the company at roughly PKR 25-30bn with a minority offer price near PKR 21-22, versus the earlier PKR 30 per share deal.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Lotte Chemicals - Everything You Need to Know about Lotte Chemicals' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Lotte's valuation in a takeover is supported by about PKR 10bn of cash and short-term investments plus roughly 150 acres of land at Port Qasim, which the analyst values in the billions of rupees.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Lotte Chemicals - Everything You Need to Know about Lotte Chemicals' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's rule is that a major negative structural development (a duty cut, an energy cost shock) obliges an investor to re-review the holding immediately, just as business owners reprice a company's earning power.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Lotte Chemicals - Everything You Need to Know about Lotte Chemicals' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst calls fertilizer defensive because gas is supplied at a policy-set rate so urea bag prices stay stable for farmers, volumes clear against matched domestic demand, and companies face little volume risk.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Fauji Fertilizer: Can It Maintain Its Strong Dividend Payout?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A fertilizer company cannot expand without first securing a gas allocation, so when no new plant is being built retained profits have little to reinvest in and payout ratios stay high.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Fauji Fertilizer: Can It Maintain Its Strong Dividend Payout?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: FFC told a corporate briefing it would maintain the roughly 75% dividend payout ratio it ran in 2025, and the analyst found first-half profit and dividend consistent with a 70-75% payout.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Fauji Fertilizer: Can It Maintain Its Strong Dividend Payout?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: FFC produces DAP evenly through the year but sells most of it in the second half because the DAP application season falls around August-September and year-end, so inventory built cheaply early can be sold into higher prices later.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Fauji Fertilizer: Can It Maintain Its Strong Dividend Payout?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst values FFC two ways: a dividend-yield approach on expected payout, and a sum-of-parts that values the fertilizer business on its earnings and then adds each investment separately.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Fauji Fertilizer: Can It Maintain Its Strong Dividend Payout?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: FFC's non-fertilizer portfolio spans listed holdings (Askari Bank, FFBL, Fauji Cement, AGP-type stakes), unlisted wind power projects, a 37.5% partnership in a Moroccan phosphoric acid plant that feeds its DAP, Thar Energy, and PIA.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Fauji Fertilizer: Can It Maintain Its Strong Dividend Payout?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's rule of thumb for valuing an independent power producer stake is to start from the equity invested, then scale it by the project's guaranteed return; Thar coal plants are cited as earning about 20%.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Fauji Fertilizer: Can It Maintain Its Strong Dividend Payout?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst declines to add FFC's cash to fair value because the unconsolidated balance sheet carries large liabilities dominated by the GIDC payable, which could absorb that cash if the case is decided against the company.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Fauji Fertilizer: Can It Maintain Its Strong Dividend Payout?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst values FFC's roughly 34% PIA stake, in which about PKR 30-35bn has been invested, at cost, treating the airline as a medium-ROIC business until results appear.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Fauji Fertilizer: Can It Maintain Its Strong Dividend Payout?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst argues PIA's returns need not match the poor global airline average because it will concentrate on diaspora, Hajj and domestic routes and pays most staff in rupees rather than international dollar salaries.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Fauji Fertilizer: Can It Maintain Its Strong Dividend Payout?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: FFC has signed an MOU for a possible urea plant of 700,000-800,000 tons capacity gasifying Thar coal, an investment of over USD 1bn that the analyst puts around 2029-2031.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Fauji Fertilizer: Can It Maintain Its Strong Dividend Payout?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Assuming Thar coal at about USD 25 a ton, the analyst estimated the coal-to-urea project's ROIC near 15%, rising towards 20% in rupee terms over 10-15 years as urea prices climb, adding roughly PKR 10 to EPS by 2030-2031.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Fauji Fertilizer: Can It Maintain Its Strong Dividend Payout?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: With domestic urea capacity already matched to demand growing 3-4% a year, Pakistan will need a new urea plant within a few years or face costly imports; building it on Thar coal rather than gas spares gas reserves and may attract green financing.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Fauji Fertilizer: Can It Maintain Its Strong Dividend Payout?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst highlighted the super tax reduction in Budget 2026 as mechanically raising listed companies' after-tax profits without any change in their operations.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Fauji Fertilizer: Can It Maintain Its Strong Dividend Payout?' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: When the 2024 removal of urea gas subsidies pushed Engro Fertilizers' SNGPL gas to PKR 1,600 while FFC and Fatima stayed at PKR 580 on direct Mari contracts, Engro's urea bag became roughly PKR 200-250 dearer than its rivals'.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why Is Engro Fertilizers Underperforming FFC? | EFERT Analysis' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The 2025 wheat crisis cut first-half urea demand, farmers switched to the cheaper bags, and Engro had to discount PKR 200-300 a bag late in the year to clear its product.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why Is Engro Fertilizers Underperforming FFC? | EFERT Analysis' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Roughly 40-42% of Pakistan's annual urea demand falls in the first six months and 58-60% in the last six, with the first-half share tied to the wheat crop.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why Is Engro Fertilizers Underperforming FFC? | EFERT Analysis' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: With industry expecting 6.5m tons of 2026 urea sales but only 3.1m sold in seven months, and Engro holding about 700,000 tons of inventory while rivals hold little, the analyst saw Engro placing 1.4-1.6m tons in the remaining months.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why Is Engro Fertilizers Underperforming FFC? | EFERT Analysis' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst scales Engro's half-year EPS by the ratio of expected volumes because depreciation and salaries are fixed, so better fixed-cost absorption adds profit beyond the volume multiple itself.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why Is Engro Fertilizers Underperforming FFC? | EFERT Analysis' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst argues urea export permission is unlikely and excludes it from forecasts: one million tons is only about two months of domestic demand, re-importing after a crisis would be politically costly, and the state could tax away the local-international price gap.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why Is Engro Fertilizers Underperforming FFC? | EFERT Analysis' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Judging urea inventory against the depressed one to two lakh tons of the black-market years is misleading: with monthly demand above 500,000 tons, two to three months of stock is normal for any industry.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why Is Engro Fertilizers Underperforming FFC? | EFERT Analysis' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst estimates Engro Fertilizers' potential GIDC payable at roughly PKR 18-20bn against about PKR 80-85bn for FFC, so a court-ordered payment hits FFC far harder in absolute terms.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why Is Engro Fertilizers Underperforming FFC? | EFERT Analysis' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: If GIDC recovery is allowed to be funded by a roughly PKR 100 bag price rise, Engro benefits proportionately more than FFC because its GIDC liability is smaller; without a price rise the analyst puts Engro's after-tax hit near PKR 10 per share.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why Is Engro Fertilizers Underperforming FFC? | EFERT Analysis' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The three fertilizer companies are jointly investing about USD 300m, with Engro's share USD 100m, in a pressure enhancement facility to sustain gas supply from the ageing Habib Rahi reservoir in Mari Energy, due to complete in Q1 2027.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why Is Engro Fertilizers Underperforming FFC? | EFERT Analysis' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Debt-funding its share of the pressure enhancement facility has raised Engro Fertilizers' borrowings, though the analyst considers the level manageable against second-half sales proceeds.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why Is Engro Fertilizers Underperforming FFC? | EFERT Analysis' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst has observed that when fertilizer companies make a large investment they petition the government for a PKR 50-100 per bag urea price increase to earn a decent return on it.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why Is Engro Fertilizers Underperforming FFC? | EFERT Analysis' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Engro Fertilizers produces roughly 2.0-2.25m tons of urea a year, about 40-45m bags, so a PKR 100 bag price change with costs unchanged moves pre-tax profit by PKR 4-4.5bn, near PKR 2 per share after tax.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Why Is Engro Fertilizers Underperforming FFC? | EFERT Analysis' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst monitors only two variables for fertilizer swing trades, the urea bag price and the gas price, because everything else (supply, seasonality) is business as usual while those two reset earning power.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Fertilizer Stocks Q&A: FFC, Engro, Fatima & How to Value Them' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's observation is that after a gas or bag price change most investors do not grasp the earnings-power shift on day one, so the share price typically takes six months to a year to reprice to the new level.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Fertilizer Stocks Q&A: FFC, Engro, Fatima & How to Value Them' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: When one producer's gas cost rose and it lifted its bag price, the other's unchanged price created a black market in the cheaper bag, and within one to two months it also raised prices, doubling its profit with no cost increase.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Fertilizer Stocks Q&A: FFC, Engro, Fatima & How to Value Them' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst decomposes fertilizer sector returns as roughly 10-12% from dividends, about 10% from rupee profit per bag rising with inflation and efficiency, and 3-4% volumetric growth tracking GDP, adding to about 20% a year.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Fertilizer Stocks Q&A: FFC, Engro, Fatima & How to Value Them' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Pakistan's urea demand has risen from about 5.5m tons a decade earlier to roughly 6.5m tons, growth absorbed by debottlenecking and by restarting Punjab LNG-based plants that used to stay idle.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Fertilizer Stocks Q&A: FFC, Engro, Fatima & How to Value Them' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Pakistani fertilizer plants are generally taken down for about a month every two years for repair and minor upgrades; FFC's three plants run three years between turnarounds, which the analyst reads as better reliability.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Fertilizer Stocks Q&A: FFC, Engro, Fatima & How to Value Them' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A fertilizer plant's nominal life is about 30 years, extendable to 50-55 with upgrades; Engro's base plant dating from the late 1960s still runs, so the analyst treats plant age as an efficiency question rather than an expiry date.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Fertilizer Stocks Q&A: FFC, Engro, Fatima & How to Value Them' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Wear and older technology show up as gas intensity: where a new plant needs about 24-25 units of gas per ton of urea an older one needs around 27, and Engro's newest plant uses roughly two units less than an FFC plant.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Fertilizer Stocks Q&A: FFC, Engro, Fatima & How to Value Them' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's valuation rule scales the required dividend yield to the payout ratio: near a 100% payout he uses roughly the interest rate plus a safety margin, around 8-9% for a 75% payer and 7-8% where payout is about 50%.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Fertilizer Stocks Q&A: FFC, Engro, Fatima & How to Value Them' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: If a company pays out materially less than roughly half its earnings, the analyst says the dividend-yield valuation framework no longer applies and another method such as a P/E approach is needed.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Fertilizer Stocks Q&A: FFC, Engro, Fatima & How to Value Them' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A new urea plant of about 1.3m tons capacity costs on the order of USD 1bn, so nobody commits that capital without a contracted government gas allocation first.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Fertilizer Stocks Q&A: FFC, Engro, Fatima & How to Value Them' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst expects an Iran-Pakistan gas pipeline to have little effect on fertilizer: a new plant would take about four years to build so nothing arrives inside six years, and cheaper gas would more likely go to industry, power or households.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Fertilizer Stocks Q&A: FFC, Engro, Fatima & How to Value Them' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's discipline is to buy only where price is well below his calculated fair value and to refuse companies trading far above it, arguing conviction comes from watching that process work two or three times.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Fertilizer Stocks Q&A: FFC, Engro, Fatima & How to Value Them' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A subsidy exists only when something is sold below its own cost, so selling gas that costs USD 5 at USD 2 is a subsidy while a rival paying more is not: subsidy has no relation to what a competitor pays.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'FAUJI FERTILIZER - Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Most Pakistani gas fields sell to SNGPL and SSGC, which recover their blended cost through consumer bills, while some fields sell directly to a customer and recover that field's own cost from it, which is why plant-level gas prices diverge.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TOP DIVIDEND STOCK IN PSX IN 2024 - FFC OR EFERT? PART 1' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: FFC's plants buy gas directly from the Mari field, whose base production cost the analyst cites at about USD 1.5 per unit, while Engro's N1 plant buys from SNGPL, so the price gap between them can persist for years.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TOP DIVIDEND STOCK IN PSX IN 2024 - FFC OR EFERT? PART 1' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: In early 2023 both FFC and Engro paid about PKR 302 per unit; SNGPL's rate was then raised while Mari stayed at 302, both were taken to PKR 580 before the first IMF review, and in March 2024 only SNGPL customers went to about PKR 1,600.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TOP DIVIDEND STOCK IN PSX IN 2024 - FFC OR EFERT? PART 1' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: IMF reviews have required gas price revision but not the elimination of the inter-company gas price disparity, and because the lower Mari rate is technically not a subsidy the government can defend keeping it.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TOP DIVIDEND STOCK IN PSX IN 2024 - FFC OR EFERT? PART 1' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's FFC thesis was that the March 2024 gas price decision, widely misread as a temporary subsidy about to be reversed, was structural and lifted FFC's earnings by roughly 50%, first visible in the Q2 2024 result.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'FAUJI FERTILIZER - Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst points to a decade in which Sindh industry paid around USD 4 for gas and Punjab 10-11, and to Punjab urea plants idled for years after being shifted to LNG, as evidence that regulated price disparities can persist.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TOP DIVIDEND STOCK IN PSX IN 2024 - FFC OR EFERT? PART 1' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Although the fertilizer industry was deregulated on paper in 2001, a complex cost-plus model still operates in practice: producers must justify any price rise with a cost increase, which also lets them pass costs on and protect profits.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TOP DIVIDEND STOCK IN PSX IN 2024 - FFC OR EFERT? PART 1' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst reasons that international urea would have to fall near USD 200 a ton to threaten Pakistani producers, which implies gas near USD 4, a level available in very few countries, so the industry is structurally protected.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TOP DIVIDEND STOCK IN PSX IN 2024 - FFC OR EFERT? PART 1' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Measured by gas index (gas needed per ton of urea), Engro's plants are estimated roughly 8-10% more efficient than FFC's, so on an equal gas rate Engro could out-earn FFC despite about 10% less capacity.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TOP DIVIDEND STOCK IN PSX IN 2024 - FFC OR EFERT? PART 1' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Engro's main N1 plant began production in 2011 and its older base plant has since been upgraded, which is why the analyst rates its efficiency above FFC's.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TOP DIVIDEND STOCK IN PSX IN 2024 - FFC OR EFERT? PART 1' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst stresses that Engro's plant must run to meet national urea demand, so the gas price gap is more likely to compress its profits for some years than to shut it down.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TOP DIVIDEND STOCK IN PSX IN 2024 - FFC OR EFERT? PART 1' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst notes Engro's earnings were defended rather than cut by the gas increase because it could justify a bag price rise to the ministry, so even a much higher gas rate could be passed into a higher bag price.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'FAUJI FERTILIZER - Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst insists investors check how secure each plant's gas supply agreement is rather than assuming renewal, citing a port operator whose share price halved when an expected contract extension did not come.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TOP DIVIDEND STOCK IN PSX - FFC OR EFERT? PART 2' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Engro's N1 plant holds a 20-year secured gas supply agreement from when it came online, with roughly 8-10 years still to run because it has received less than contracted volumes, while the base plant runs on an as-and-when-available basis.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TOP DIVIDEND STOCK IN PSX - FFC OR EFERT? PART 2' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst treats gas supply agreements and gas pricing as two separate questions that should not be conflated: a contract renewal does not imply a price revision, and the government can change price at any time regardless.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TOP DIVIDEND STOCK IN PSX - FFC OR EFERT? PART 2' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's rule is to estimate FFC's dividend from unconsolidated earnings, because earnings from its stakes in other companies do not necessarily arrive as cash dividends to FFC itself.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TOP DIVIDEND STOCK IN PSX - FFC OR EFERT? PART 2' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst attributes FFC's payout slipping towards 70-75% of unconsolidated earnings to funding gas supply investments from its own cash rather than debt, and to a GIDC balance roughly four to five times Engro's.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TOP DIVIDEND STOCK IN PSX - FFC OR EFERT? PART 2' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Interest income on FFC's large cash and fixed-income balances contributes roughly 10-20% of its earnings depending on the policy rate, making its profits partly rate-sensitive.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TOP DIVIDEND STOCK IN PSX - FFC OR EFERT? PART 2' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst never forecasts a change in dividend policy: owners set it, it typically persists two to three years once changed, so an investment case should not rest on an expected future payout increase.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TOP DIVIDEND STOCK IN PSX - FFC OR EFERT? PART 2' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's dividend framework: a forward yield near 20% can give both income and 10-20% capital gain if rates fall to around 15%, for a 30-40% total return, whereas a 15-16% yield likely delivers income with little re-rating.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TOP DIVIDEND STOCK IN PSX - FFC OR EFERT? PART 2' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst ranks each candidate's expected total return against his other holdings and invests only where it falls among the top five to seven ideas, a concept of best available investments.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TOP DIVIDEND STOCK IN PSX - FFC OR EFERT? PART 2' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Zinc urea normally sells at a premium that merely covers the zinc coating cost, but while official urea was capped below the black-market rate it let Engro capture a far larger premium per bag and lift profits sharply.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TOP DIVIDEND STOCK IN PSX - FFC OR EFERT? PART 2' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's benchmark is that urea producers earn roughly PKR 1,200-1,500 of pre-tax profit on a normal bag, so any product able to add a comparable premium can double per-bag profit.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TOP DIVIDEND STOCK IN PSX - FFC OR EFERT? PART 2' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The transmission rule the analyst draws is that whenever Pakistani urea is short and the market price runs above the official price, producers selling premium variants such as zinc urea capture that gap as extra margin.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'TOP DIVIDEND STOCK IN PSX - FFC OR EFERT? PART 2' (YouTube transcript, undated)
